name: Os_IpcQueryCommand18
summary: Leaf IPC query on the SDK's shared session: writes command header 0x00180000 (command 0x18, no parameters) into the thread's IPC buffer and issues SVC 0x32 (SendSyncRequest); on success it copies the eight response words out and returns the reply result code. Used by the date/time query path.
evidence: mrc p15,0,r4,c13,c0,3 (TPIDRURO) then str 0x180000,[r4,#0x80] (IPC buffer at TLS+0x80), svc #0x32 = SendSyncRequest per 3dbrew SVC table, result at TLS+0x84, 8 words TLS+0x88..0xA4 copied to arg2. Caller 0x0011F5C0 ('Os_QueryTime') parses the 8 words as a calendar value and 0x00119B4C re-exports them.

name: std_Strncmp
signature: int std_Strncmp(const u8* a, const u8* b, u32 len, u32 aligned)
summary: Bounded string compare. While four or more bytes remain it compares whole words, using a saturating per-byte subtract against the 0x01010101 constant to detect a NUL terminator, and falls back to a byte loop for the tail; returns the difference of the first mismatching bytes (or +-1 after a byte-swapped ordering compare).
evidence: Word loop compares 4 bytes, UQSUB8 (UnsignedSaturate) against literal 0x0012374C = 0x01010101 detects 0x00, returns (word_a&0xff)-(word_b&0xff) etc.; the differing-word path compares bswap(a)<bswap(b) i.e. memory byte order; tail loop advances 2 bytes at a time while bytes are equal and non-zero; arg4 bit0..1 selects the aligned fast path.

name: Os_IpcSendCommand0E
summary: Two-parameter IPC request: command 0x0E with two normal words (value, 0xA|value<<4) and one translate buffer descriptor (buffer). Returns the reply result code.
evidence: Header literal 0x00123C94 = 0x000E0042 (cmd 0x0E, 2 normal + 1 translate parameter), TLS+0x84 = value, TLS+0x88 = 0xA|(value<<4) buffer descriptor, TLS+0x8C = buffer, svc #0x32 SendSyncRequest on the handle in *0x007B2D2C (same session as 0x00123D68/0x00123508).

name: Os_IpcSendCommand0D
summary: Two-parameter IPC request: command 0x0D with two normal words (value, 0x2|value<<14) and one translate buffer descriptor (buffer). Sibling of 0x00123C54; 0x001228AC picks between the two.
evidence: Header literal 0x00123DAC = 0x000D0042 (cmd 0x0D, 2 normal + 1 translate), TLS+0x84 = value, TLS+0x88 = 2|(value<<14), TLS+0x8C = buffer, svc #0x32. Caller 0x001228AC compares a value and branches to 0x00123C54 (0x0E) or this one (0x0D).

name: maybe_Os_TranslateMainRamRangeB

name: maybe_std_UnwindPersonalityRoutine
signature: u32 maybe_std_UnwindPersonalityRoutine(void* state, void* ucb, void* context)
summary: ARM EHABI personality/trampoline routine: calls the unwind bytecode interpreter at 0x001250BC (which reads the inline opcode words that follow the call) and returns an unwind reason code. The region 0x00125098-0x00125738 is the C++ exception-unwinding support code, not game code.

Also called from 0x00723E7C / 0x00723EF0 at the end of .text, which are further personality-routine fragments. Ghidra merged the whole block into one 'function'.

name: std_MemcpyForward32
signature: void* std_MemcpyForward32(void* dst, const void* src, u32 size)
summary: Aligned forward memcpy: moves 32 bytes per iteration with ldm/stm plus a pld prefetch, then handles 16/8/4/2/1-byte tails. Returns the end pointers (src_end in r1, dst_end in r0).
evidence: ldm r1!,{r4-r7}; ldm r1!,{r8,sb,sl,lr}; pld [r1,#0x40]; stm r0!,{...}; subs r2,#0x20 loop, then 16/8/4/2/1 tails. Companion of the shifted variants 0x001257C4/0x00125860/0x001258FC and of the backward family 0x00125AD4..0x00125C90.

name: std_MemcpyForwardShift8
signature: void* std_MemcpyForwardShift8(void* dst, const void* src, u32 size)
summary: Forward memcpy for a destination one byte past word alignment: reads 8 words and re-emits them shifted by 8 bits, carrying the top byte into the next word; same 32/16/8/4/2/1 tail structure as std_MemcpyForward32.
evidence: in_r12|uVar6<<8, arg1[n]=uVar6>>24|uVar7<<8 ... exactly a byte-shift-8 word stream; loop count 0x20 at a time; returns (src_end,dst_end). Sits in the unrolled memcpy family after 0x00125738 and before 0x00125860 (shift 16) / 0x001258FC (shift 24).

name: std_MemcpyForwardShift16
signature: void* std_MemcpyForwardShift16(void* dst, const void* src, u32 size)
summary: Forward memcpy for a destination two bytes off word alignment: shifts the source words by 16 bits while copying, with the usual 32/16/8/4/2/1 tails.
evidence: Word stream `in_r12|uVar6<<0x10` and `uVar6>>0x10|uVar7<<0x10`; sibling of 0x001257C4 (<<8) and 0x001258FC (>>8), all returning end pointers.

name: std_MemcpyForwardShift24

signature: void* std_MemmoveBackward32(void* dst_end, const void* src_end, u32 size)

summary: Compiler VFP context helper (two entry labels): saves d8-d15 into a caller buffer / restores them, used by the soft-float and exception-support code. Ghidra merged the save and restore halves into one 'function' because the save half ends in bx lr but the restore half follows immediately.

name: std_DoubleDivideCore
signature: u64 std_DoubleDivideCore(u32 q_lo, u32 n_hi, u32 n_lo, u32 d_hi, u32 d_lo)
summary: Software double-precision division core: normalises the operands with a reciprocal byte table, runs the Newton-Raphson quotient refinement and the four 16-bit long-division steps, then assembles the result exponent/mantissa. Only reachable from the soft-float helpers around it.
evidence: ldrb from table 0x00126610 (indexed by the divisor's top byte), `rsb r7,r7,#0x800000; mul r6,r7,r6; lsr r6,#0x13` Newton step, then repeated 16-bit limb multiply/subtract with the carry flags, returning CONCAT44(exponent, arg1). Neighbour 0x00126848 is already named std_DoubleDivide and 0x00126878 std_DoubleMultiply, which hand off to this core family.

name: std_ScalbnDouble
signature: double std_ScalbnDouble(u32 lo, u32 hi, u32 mant, int exponent)
summary: Double-precision scalbn/ldexp: shifts the mantissa by the requested exponent and rebuilds the IEEE-754 word, returning the input unchanged when the resulting exponent field stays inside the normal range (0x000-0x7FF).
evidence: Calls 0x0012676C with (lo, hi>>0xb, mant, exponent-1) then checks `((result & 0x7fffffff)+1) < 0x800` - the 11-bit IEEE double exponent range - and adds the delta into the exponent with a 0x100000 mantissa shift. Overflow path returns the constant g_00126768.

name: maybe_std_ScalbnRoundTail
signature: double maybe_std_ScalbnRoundTail(u32 sign, u32 hi, u32 mant, int exponent)
summary: Rounding/overflow tail of the double scalbn helper: increments the exponent, propagates a carry into the mantissa and sets the sign bit, saturating to infinity. Reached by branch from the scalbn code, not a stand-alone API.
evidence: Uses the incoming flags (unaff_r11, in_CY) to detect mantissa overflow, adds 1 to the exponent (`arg2+1`), saturates to 0x80000000, and returns CONCAT44(hi, exponent+(0|1) | sign&0x80000000). Branch target 0x001267CC lies inside 0x00126728's range.

name: std_DoubleMultiplyCore
signature: u64 std_DoubleMultiplyCore(u32 p_lo, u32 a_hi, u32 a_lo, u32 b_hi, u32 b_lo)
summary: Software double-precision multiply core: splits both operands into 16-bit limbs, accumulates the cross products with carry propagation, applies the sign correction and returns the normalised 64-bit product. Companion of std_DoubleDivideCore.
evidence: Six 16-bit limb multiplies with `CARRY4` carry fix-ups (`uVar8*uVar14`, `uVar6*uVar8`, `uVar12*uVar6` ...), then subtracts the two signs (`arg2-arg3`, `unaff_r4-unaff_r5`) and returns CONCAT44(mantissa_hi, arg1). Branch target 0x001265CE is inside 0x001263E4's divide core, so the two are the mul/div halves of the same soft-double unit.
